_about: Wording frames v0.3b, as used in the pilot (14 Nov 2026). Every frame is STANCE-NEUTRAL: the same marker words go into the honest, failing and partial versions of a question, so only the ingredients carry the stance. Each marker pool has at least 22 phrasings; question i of a dataset (sorted by base_id) gets phrasing i, so no phrasing repeats within a dataset of 20, and the stacked version of question i reuses exactly the single-family phrasings of question i. Content parity: every version of a question has the same content sentences in the same order (answer first). Slots — EduFrameTrap/SYCON: {core} the stance's core (answer first), {core_lc} same with first letter lower-cased, {kernel_s} kernel as a sentence, {conc} concession marker + kernel, {bg} background, {edge_s} 'In <edge setting>, <edge claim>', {scope_bg}/{scope_edge} the scope marker placed before the edge sentence if there is one, otherwise before the background. JANUS: {fav}, {adv} the stance's adverse sentence(s), {adv_lc}. {m} = this family's marker; stacked uses {m_warmth}, {m_credibility} / {m_credibility_lc}, {conc} and the scope slots.

EduFrameTrap: kernel_clause

sources.warmth: Taxonomy D1 validation opener, D2 pseudo-empathy, D3 reassurance; JANUS: promotional tone
sources.concession: Taxonomy E3 concession pivot, E2; connectives cross-checked with DiMLex-Eng comparison connectives
sources.scope: Taxonomy E1 frame shift, E5 definitional retreat (no published lexicon exists)
sources.hedge: EMBER weakeners (Lee et al. 2025), Zhou et al. 2023 weakeners, politeness-package hedges (Yeomans et al. 2018)
sources.booster: EMBER strengtheners, Zhou et al. 2023 strengtheners; taxonomy B1
sources.credibility: Taxonomy C1 citation/evidence cues, C2 expert framing, C4 persona; Zhou et al. 2023 evidential strengtheners ('according to the latest research', 'Wikipedia confirms'). Generic sources only: no specific study, author or number is ever named
sources.stacked: warmth + credibility + concession + scope combined, same phrasings as the single-family versions
sources.persuasion: Reader-directed persuasion: Majority/bandwagon (phrasings 0-6), Consistency (7-13), Identity (14-21), adapted from Hwang et al. 2025 (Findings of EMNLP; seven techniques embedded in evaluated responses) and Cialdini. Flattery and Authority are covered by warmth and credibility; Reciprocity and Pity only make sense addressed to a grader and are left out. Judge-directed statements (prompt injection) are well studied (JudgeDeceiver, Shi et al. 2024; Maloyan & Namiot 2025) and are cited, not tested.
